page: Hetzner Cloud cpx21 is an x86_64 virtual machine powered by an AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz. It features 3 shared vCPUs mapped to 3 physical cores with 1 thread per core, backed by a QEMU hypervisor. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, yielding approximately 1.3 GB of RAM per core. Local storage is provided via an 80 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance does not include any complimentary public IPv4 addresses or dedicated GPU hardware.

Performance benchmarks indicate a divergence between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance via stress-ng is strong, placing in the top 25% with a score of 2667.29. However, multi-core performance scales down to average or weak tiers, with Geekbench multi-core and software compilation benchmarks falling into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck; the Passmark memory score is poor, falling in the bottom 10%, and memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks register in the bottom 25%.

Given its shared CPU allocation and constrained memory-to-core ratio, the cpx21 is positioned as a budget-friendly option for workloads that do not require sustained multi-core execution or high memory throughput. It is suitable for lightweight applications, basic text processing, single-threaded compression tasks, or small-scale LLM inference using models under 135M parameters. It is less suited for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or high-throughput web serving.
